chapter_name: Change and Development in Rural Society
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the complex class structures of Indian villages, the impact of land reforms, the Green Revolution, and how farmers connect to the global market!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In rural India, class (how much land you own) and caste are deeply intertwined. Dominant castes usually own the most land, while lower castes often work as landless agricultural laborers.
Post-independence laws aimed to distribute land more fairly. They abolished the Zamindari system and introduced land ceiling acts, though implementation was very uneven across states.
A 1960s program introducing High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides. It made India self-sufficient in food but mainly benefited rich farmers and worsened regional inequalities.
Commercialization of agriculture led to farmers hiring cheap migrant labor instead of local workers. This created 'footloose labour'—poor workers constantly moving to find seasonal harvesting jobs.

fun_activity.title: 🍅 The Grocery Supply Chain
fun_activity.instructions: Take a packet of branded chips or ketchup from your kitchen. Trace its journey backward: from your hands, to the supermarket, to the factory, and finally to the contract farmers who grew the potatoes or tomatoes!

exam_tips: 📌 Always mention Jan Breman's concept of 'footloose labour' when discussing the circulation of labor.
📌 Be ready to evaluate the Green Revolution critically—know both its successes (food security) and failures (environmental damage, inequality).
📌 Farmer suicides are deeply linked to the shift toward expensive cash crops and debt traps in a globalized economy.
quick_recap: ⭐ The abolition of the Zamindari system was the most successful of the land reforms.
⭐ Contract farming brings modern technology to farmers but leaves them vulnerable to the demands of multinational corporations.
⭐ Rural society is moving away from traditional, hereditary relationships (like the Jajmani system) to formal, cash-based work.
